title: In Memoriam: Hank Leiber remembered on his birthday (January 17) - Tucson Standard
text:
Henry Edward Leiber was born on January 17, 1911, in Tucson, Arizona. His parents raised him in a sports-loving environment. From a young age, Henry showed an interest in baseball. He developed his skills and became a talented player.
Leiber made his Major League Baseball debut in 1933 with the New York Giants. He played as an outfielder and quickly became known for his batting skills. He was a strong hitter and contributed significantly to his team’s success. In 1939, he was traded to the Chicago Cubs, where he continued to perform well. Leiber’s career spanned from 1933 to 1942, during which he played in many important games and made a name for himself in the league.
Throughout his career, Leiber maintained a connection to Tucson. He often returned to his hometown, where he was a local hero. He supported local baseball programs and inspired young players with his achievements.
After retiring from baseball in 1942, Leiber continued to live in Tucson. He remained active in the community, sharing his love for the sport. Henry Edward Leiber died on November 8, 1993, in Tucson. His life and career left a lasting impact on the baseball community and his hometown.
Henry Leiber’s story is one of dedication and passion for baseball. His achievements on the field and his connection to Tucson are remembered and celebrated by many. His legacy as a player and a mentor continues to inspire future generations.
